kjv: I (Yahweh) will corrupt your (the priests') seed
mine: I (Yahweh) am going to rebuke your (the priests') offspring
note: Hebrew go'er means "rebuke" (threaten, check); the LXX/Vulgate read zeroa' ("arm") and "cut off". "Corrupt" matches neither the Hebrew verb nor the versions.

Hebrew 'er we'oneh, literally "one who rouses and one who answers", is an obscure idiom generally taken as an all-inclusive pair ("anyone at all"); the KJV's "master and scholar" follows a rabbinic guess (teacher and pupil).

kjv: And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one?
mine: Did not the One make you, and is not a remnant of spirit his? And what was the One seeking?
note: One of the most obscure verses in the OT; the Hebrew welo'-'echad 'asah ushe'ar ruach lo can mean "did not one (God) make (them)" or "no one would do (this) who had a remnant of spirit". Both renderings are attempts; the KJV takes "one" as the one flesh of marriage.

kjv: he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment
mine: For the man who hates and divorces ... covers his garment with violence
note: Hebrew ki-sane' shallach has a third-person participle ("one hating"), not "I hate"; it can mean "(he) hates divorce" or describe the man who rejects and divorces his wife. The second clause is wekhissah chamas 'al-levusho, "covers his garment with violence" (violence stains him), which the KJV reverses. Context: the man who hates and divorces covers his garment with violence (medium confidence). Sane' is third person ('one hating'), not 'I hate', and the LXX, 4QXIIa, Targum and Vulgate all make the husband the subject. This continues 2:14-15 and fits the closing 'do not be faithless'. Yet a divine statement 'I hate divorce' is widely held, and the syntax is difficult. Other possible meanings: (1) 'For I hate divorce / he hates divorce, says Yahweh' — KJV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS, NET, as God's own attitude; (2) 'if you hate her, divorce her' (permission, cf. Deut 24:1) — 4QXIIa, Targum, Vulgate, LXX 'if you hate and send away'; (3) 'covers violence with his garment' — KJV, reversing the image.
